title: Maximum Value Sum by Placing Three Rooks I
statement: You get an `m x n` grid `board` of integers, where `board[i][j]` is the value written on the cell in row `i` and column `j`. A rook threatens every other cell of its row and of its column. Put exactly three rooks on the board so that none of them threatens another, which means the three rooks stand in three different rows and in three different columns. Return the largest possible total of the values of the three cells that hold a rook. Values can be negative, so this total can be negative as well.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every triple of rows already costs about m³/6 · 27 checks. But a rook only has to dodge the two columns of the other rooks, so in any row its best usable cell is among that row's three largest cells; likewise, in a band of rows `0..r` it lies in one of the band's three best columns. So enumerate the middle rook's row and combine three candidates above it, three in it and three below it. Swapping each rook of a valid placement for its best allowed candidate never lowers the total, so one of these combinations is optimal.

## Approach

1. `keepThree(cells)` sorts `[value, col]` pairs, largest first, and keeps the first three with different columns.
2. `top[r]` is that list for row `r`. `above[r]` merges `above[r - 1]` with `top[r]` (rows `0..r`), and `below[r]` merges `below[r + 1]` with `top[r]` (rows `r..m-1`).
3. For each middle row `mid` from 1 to `m - 2`, combine every `[v1, c1]` of `above[mid - 1]`, `[v2, c2]` of `top[mid]` and `[v3, c3]` of `below[mid + 1]`, skip repeated columns, and keep the largest `v1 + v2 + v3` in `best`. Rows cannot clash: the rooks are above, in and below `mid`.

## Example 1, step by step

`m = 3`, so only `mid = 1` is tried. `above[0]` holds row 0's 1s (columns 1 to 3), `top[1]` holds row 1's 1s (columns 1 and 3) and a -3, and `below[2]` holds row 2's 2 (column 1) and its 1s (columns 2 and 3). Taking the 2 below forces the other rooks off column 1: the 1 in column 2 above and the 1 in column 3 of row 1, so `best = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · n log n): each row is sorted once; a merge sorts at most 6 cells and each `mid` tries at most 27 combinations.
- Space: O(m + n): three cells per row and band, plus one row while it is sorted.

## Pitfalls

- Keeping only each row's best cell fails: in Test 2 every row's best value is in column 0.
- A merged band must keep one cell per column; three cells from one column are useless once it is taken.
- Start `best` at `-Infinity`, since every value may be negative.
- Totals reach 3 · 10^9, beyond 32-bit integers (`long` in Java, `long long` in C).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `keepThree` | keeps the three best cells that lie in different columns |
| `top[r]` | the three best cells of row `r`, as `[value, col]` |
| `above[r]`, `below[r]` | the three best columns over rows `0..r` and over rows `r..m-1` |
| `mid` | row of the middle rook |
| `v1, c1`, `v2, c2`, `v3, c3` | value and column of the rook above `mid`, in `mid` and below `mid` |
| `best` | largest total found so far |

narration.2: m is the number of rows.
narration.3: keepThree shrinks a list of [value, col] cells to its three best cells in different columns.
narration.4: Sort the cells so the largest values come first.
narration.6: Scan the cells from the largest value down.
narration.7: Keep a cell while fewer than three are kept and no kept cell already uses its column.
narration.9: Three columns are enough, because a rook only ever has to avoid the two columns of the other rooks.
narration.12: For every row, keep its three best cells as [value, col] pairs.
narration.13: The band of rows above starts with row 0 alone.
narration.15: Merge the band so far with row r: the three best columns over rows 0..r.
narration.18: The band of rows below starts with the last row alone.
narration.20: Merge from the bottom up: the three best columns over rows r..m-1.
narration.23: No placement tried yet; values may be negative, so start below every possible total.
narration.24: Choose the row of the middle rook; there must be a row above it and a row below it.
narration.25: First rook: one of the three best columns anywhere above mid.
narration.26: Second rook: one of the three best cells of row mid.
narration.27: Skip it when it shares the first rook's column.
narration.28: Third rook: one of the three best columns anywhere below mid.
narration.29: Skip it when it shares a column with either other rook.
narration.30: The three rooks are safe from each other: keep the largest total.
narration.35: Every middle row has been tried; return the best total.
